_verificationNote: AUDITED 2026-08-15 — TWO DIFFERENT THINGS LIVE IN THIS FILE. (A) THE AGE CURVE IS REAL AND VERIFIED EXACTLY. All 65 ageFactorsPermille values were diffed programmatically against Appendix I of the CCIIO Insurance Standards Bulletin 'Guidance Regarding Age Curves and State Reporting' (16 Dec 2016), fetched from https://www.cms.gov/cciio/resources/regulations-and-guidance/downloads/final-guidance-regarding-age-curves-and-state-reporting-12-16-16.pdf on 2026-08-15: ZERO mismatches (0-14 = 0.765, 15 = 0.833, 20 = 0.970, 21-24 = 1.000, 25 = 1.004, ... 63 = 2.952, 64 and older = 3.000). The 3:1 cap and the age-band structure are confirmed by 45 C.F.R. §147.102(a)(1)(iii) and (d), fetched from https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title45-vol2/xml/CFR-2025-title45-vol2-sec147-102.xml — single band 0-14, one-year bands 15-20, one-year bands 21-63, single band '64 AND OLDER'. The key '64' therefore means 64-and-older: any code path that can receive age 65+ must clamp to 64 rather than fall through. Per §147.102(e) this is only a DEFAULT, applying where a state has not established its own curve; CMS's State Specific Rating Variations table shows NEW YORK and VERMONT at a 1:1 individual-market age ratio, meaning premiums there do not vary by age AT ALL — applying this curve to a NY or VT enrollee would be materially wrong. That table is stamped 'Updated December 10, 2021' and no newer version exists, so current per-state curves remain UNRESOLVED. (B) THE SIX COUNTY PREMIUMS ARE INVENTED AND WERE NOT VERIFIED — there is nothing to verify. They must be replaced, not checked. PRODUCTION SOURCE LOCATED, PY2026 URLs confirmed live (HTTP 200, application/zip): https://download.cms.gov/marketplace-puf/2026/rate-puf.zip (per-plan premium by rating area and individual age), .../plan-attributes-puf.zip (metal level, on/off-exchange), .../service-area-puf.zip (county FIPS to rating area), landing page https://www.cms.gov/marketplace/resources/data/public-use-files . PIPELINE: join Rate x Plan Attributes x Service Area to get the Silver plans actually available in each county, sort by premium, take the second lowest. FOUR TRAPS: (1) the PUFs cover only HealthCare.gov states — the ~20 State-Based Marketplaces including CALIFORNIA, which is in the sample list below, publish separately or not at all, so a single national ingest fails for roughly a third of the population; (2) do NOT keep the age21Base x ageFactor model — the Rate PUF gives the premium at each age directly, and storing that eliminates the NY/VT problem above entirely; (3) SLCSP is a per-county ranking that can flip when one issuer exits, so it must be re-ingested annually, never patched; (4) a rating area can span multiple counties, so join on rating area and then map to counties, never the reverse. Until this lands, the SAMPLE_DATA status and the UI's sample-data labelling are the only things between a user and a fabricated dollar figure — keep both. CITATION HYGIENE: the ecfr.gov URL below is bot-blocked; prefer the govinfo CFR URL above. WHERE TO RE-CHECK ANNUALLY: new PUFs appear at download.cms.gov/marketplace-puf/{year}/ around October-November for the following plan year. See VERIFICATION-STATUS.md.
